segments.en: That's right.

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
Today in Language Takeaway we have a number of phrases and words about business.
segments.zh: 今天在语言要点中，我们有许多关于商业的短语和单词。

segments.en: The first one we have is, are you joining the conference today?
segments.zh: 我们拥有的第一个是，您今天参加会议吗？

segments.en: That's right.
So we're going to go to a conference, actually, which is a little bit different than a meeting.
segments.zh: 所以我们要去参加一个会议，实际上，这与会议有点不同。

segments.en: That's right. A meeting is something you normally do with people at your own company. But a conference is when people from many different companies meet.
segments.zh: 没错。 会议是您通常与自己公司的人进行的事情。 但会议是来自许多不同公司的人见面的时候。

segments.en: That's right. And also, I think you don't really have too much input at a conference.
segments.zh: 没错。而且，我认为在大会上你其实没有太多发言的机会。

segments.en: You mostly listen to other people speak about a topic or a subject.
segments.zh: 你主要听别人谈论一个话题或一个主题。

segments.en: That's right.
And I think these are normally held in conference centers or hotels.
segments.zh: 我认为这些通常在会议中心或酒店举行。

segments.en: You have a nice lunch.
So they're pretty big deals.
segments.zh: 所以它们是相当重要的活动。

segments.en: That's right. All right, so it's more of a formal business conference that we're going to.
segments.zh: 没错。 好吧，所以它更像是一个正式的商务会议。

segments.en: And well, they're actually going to discuss different aspects of the company as well, especially the figures.
segments.zh: 好吧，他们实际上也将讨论公司的不同方面，尤其是数字。

segments.en: All right.
So in the context of business, the word figure actually means number.
segments.zh: 所以在商业的背景下，数字这个词实际上意味着数字。

segments.en: Okay, so we can say the sales numbers for this year are a kind of figure.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们可以说今年的销售数据是一种数字。

segments.en: That's right.
So we're talking about money, basically, when we're talking about numbers.
segments.zh: 所以我们谈论的是金钱，基本上，当我们谈论数字时。

segments.en: That's right. So when the figures look good, it means that our income, our revenue, this looks good.
segments.zh: 没错。所以当这些数字看起来不错时，意味着我们的收入、我们的营收看起来不错。

segments.en: That's right. And when we usually talk about income or revenue, we usually have to separate it into time.
segments.zh: 没错。而且我们谈收入或营收时，通常得把它按时间段来划分。

segments.en: And here in the dialogue, we're talking about a quarter.
segments.zh: 在对话里，我们说的是一个季度。

segments.en: All right, so quarter, Q-U, quarter, is a period of time, very common in business, that is a quarter of the year.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以季度，Q-U，季度，是一个时期，在商业中很常见，也就是一年中的一个季度。

segments.en: So three months.
Three months, that's right.
January, February, March, April, May, June, and so on.
segments.zh: 一月、二月、三月、四月、五月、六月等等。

segments.en: That's right. So you have four quarters.
segments.zh: 没错。 所以你有四个季度。

segments.en: And that's actually what, that's why you call it a quarter because it's one fourth.
segments.zh: 正因如此，你才把它叫做 quarter，因为它是四分之一。

segments.en: So we can say the figures for the first quarter were very good, but unfortunately, the figures for the second quarter were very bad.
segments.zh: 所以我们可以说第一季度的数据非常好，但不幸的是，第二季度的数据非常糟糕。

segments.en: That's right.
And actually, another similar way that you use quarter is the 25 cent coin.
segments.zh: 实际上，quarter 的另一个类似用法是 25 美分硬币。

segments.en: It's called a quarter because it's a quarter of a dollar.
segments.zh: 它之所以叫 quarter，是因为它是四分之一美元。

segments.en: That's right. And if you're in America, you know that it has an eagle, a bird on one side of it.
segments.zh: 没错。 如果你在美国，你知道它有一只鹰，一只鸟在它的一侧。

segments.en: That's right.
All right, so we are taking a look at the figures for the quarter.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们正在查看本季度的数据。

segments.en: And they're saying, well, it's not looking too good because we need to talk about the advertising budget.
segments.zh: 他们说，好吧，这看起来不太好，因为我们需要谈谈广告预算。

segments.en: All right.
So this is something that you think is very important.
segments.zh: 所以这是你认为非常重要的事情。

segments.en: It's budget.
It's how much money you have to spend on something.
segments.zh: 它是你花在某件事上的钱的数额。

segments.en: And in this case, you're spending it on advertising.
segments.zh: 在这种情况下，你把它花在广告上。

segments.en: So this is ads that you make.
segments.zh: 所以这是你制作的广告。

segments.en: That's right.
So as you said, a budget is the amount of money that you have available to spend on something.
segments.zh: 所以正如你所说，预算是你可以花在某物上的金额。

segments.en: And on this occasion, we're talking about advertising.
segments.zh: 在这个场合，我们谈论的是广告。

segments.en: Now, you can have a budget for different things, right?
segments.zh: 现在，你可以为不同的事情制定预算，对吧？

segments.en: You could have a marketing budget.
So the money you have for marketing.
You could have a personnel budget, which is the money you would set aside for people.
segments.zh: 你可以有人事预算，也就是你为员工预留的钱。

segments.en: So how much you pay your employees. Right. So you can pretty much mix up many different nouns with budget.
segments.zh: 也就是你付给员工多少钱。对。所以你几乎可以把很多不同的名词和 budget 搭配使用。

segments.en: Even you can have a budget for your home.
segments.zh: 即使你可以为你的家制定预算。

segments.en: How much you spend at home.
That's right. So many people have this for their families.
segments.zh: 没错。很多人家里都会做这样的预算。

segments.en: They say this month I will spend $100 on shopping and $200 on shoes.
segments.zh: 他们说这个月我要花 100 美元购物，200 美元买鞋。

segments.en: So it's like a family budget, you would call it.
segments.zh: 所以你会把它叫做家庭预算。

segments.en: That's right. Okay. So that's all the words we have for you on language takeaway.
segments.zh: 没错。 好的。 这就是我们在语言要点中为您准备的所有单词。

How's the family?

segments.zh: 但这是一个很短的表达方式。

segments.en: It's very common.

segments.zh: 实际上，这句话的构成方式可能看起来有点怪，但它和 How are you? 非常相似。
